newsitem.title: UK: Copper finishes higher, but LME rangebound.
newsitem.headline: Copper finishes higher, but LME rangebound.

text.p: Copper prices perked up in late Tuesday LME trading but conditions throughout the complex were fairly low-key and traders said that the red metal looked to be favouring a range-trading pattern.

Latest LME stock data showed a 5,400-tonne increase, which was the higher end of expectations, but was not construed as a great surprise. Recent inventory movements have all been much as expected, and with stocks now on an upward curve, market volatility has subsided this week, traders added.
"It has been very slow today and there has been an element of "winding down" ahead of the year-end," one analyst said.
Copper prices were reasonably well defended on dips below $2,120, as was the case late last week, and this area down to $2,100 is seen forming the lower level of a $50 technical range, traders said.
Next week's "third Wednesday" hurdle remains to be overcome, but there is less concern over the December date now, compared to two weeks ago, as many positions have been squared off.
Final three months business on the kerb was at $2,136 a tonne, up $3 from Monday's kerb. The cash/threes backwardation narrowed to around $138 from $162 yesterday.
Elsewhere, there was little excitement in the other metals, although aluminium lost ground, while tin and lead notched up fresh lows for the current downswing.

Aluminium gradually fell away towards the $1,500 support level, paying little attention to a LME warehouse stock fall or IPAI producer inventory decline, both of which had been expected. Last trade was at $1,503.50, down $5.50.
Tin suffered from investment fund liquidation, against a backdrop of recent Chinese and Malaysian selling, as well as rising LME inventories.

The market dropped to a fresh 1-1/2 year low of $5,760 before ending at $5,770, down $70. Nickel was not helped by a 564-tonne stock increase, although price declines were fairly light, given the general slow conditions. Last trade was at $6,800, down $20.
Lead inched up after earlier equalling Monday's 13-month lows of $666, as this is important trend-line support.
But the overall outlook remains gloomy, unless there is a severe cold snap in the Northern Hemisphere. Prices closed at $672, a $5.50 gain.
The zinc market was sluggish throughout, but was aided by a 2,425-tonne fall in stocks. Three months closed at $1,045, up $3 from the previous close.
Aluminium alloy held around overnight levels, closing at a steady $1,352/54 a tonne.
